stops.note: likely the ultimate source of the word for the mineral flux
adopted from Persian and applied to various flux substances used in metalworking
borrowed from Arabic alchemical and mineralogical texts
entered English via Anglo-French 'boras' as the name of the mineral
stops.meaning: a white mineral used in cleaning and glassmaking

stops.note: coined by Humphry Davy by blending 'borax' with the ending of 'carbon', since the two elements share properties

current_meaning: a hard, brittle metalloid chemical element
